home.metaTitle: analysisACE: FIRE planning and personal finance for Bangladesh
home.subtitle: Plan financial independence in Bangla and English: your FIRE number, savings rate and projected FIRE age, built on your Assets, Capital and Earnings, with Zakat, tax and halal choices included.

hero.eyebrow: FIRE planning for families in Bangladesh
hero.title: Find the year work becomes optional.
hero.lead: analysisACE turns your household's income, costs and savings into a FIRE plan: your FIRE number, your savings rate and the year your capital could cover your costs. Grow your Assets, Capital and Earnings, with Zakat, tax and halal choices built in. Every number shows where it came from.

fire.title: Financial independence in three ideas
fire.lead: FIRE means Financial Independence, Retire Early. You are financially independent when your invested capital could pay your family's yearly costs. Retiring early is optional; the freedom is the point.

number.title: Your FIRE number
number.body: Add up a year of your household's real costs and multiply by 25. That is roughly the invested capital that could pay for those costs every year at a 4% withdrawal rate.

rate.title: Your savings rate
rate.body: The share of income you keep. It works twice: it builds capital faster, and it lowers the costs your capital has to cover.

date.title: Your FIRE date
date.body: The age at which your investable capital is projected to reach your FIRE number, from your own savings, returns and inflation. Progress updates as your records grow.

fire.formula: FIRE number = a year of costs × 25
fire.formulaNote: 25 is 100 ÷ 4, the 4% withdrawal rate. You can change the rate in your plan. It is a rule of thumb from past markets, not a guarantee.

rate.title: Your savings rate decides more than your returns
rate.lead: Returns are mostly outside your control. What you keep from each month's income is not.
rate.body: In this illustration, moving from saving 20% to 40% of income shortens the wait by about 15 years. analysisACE works out your savings rate from your income and cost records every month.
rate.chartTitle: Years from zero to FIRE, by savings rate
rate.assumptions: Illustration, not a forecast. Starts from zero savings and assumes a 5% yearly return after inflation and a 4% withdrawal rate. Your own plan uses your figures.

local.title: A FIRE plan made for life here
local.lead: Most FIRE calculators assume low inflation and an index fund. Families here face different facts, and the plan handles them.

inflation.title: Inflation from BBS figures

home.body: Land and the family home are left out of the money you can live from by default, because they cannot be sold a piece at a time. You can include them.

zakat.title: Zakat inside the plan
zakat.body: Zakat is worked out line by line each year, and the Zakat and sadaqah you record as costs are part of your FIRE number.

stress.title: Tested against bad years
stress.body: See your plan after a market fall in year one, higher costs, higher inflation, stopping work five years sooner, or a replay of a past DSE event.

own.title: Our own screen
own.body: analysisACE runs its own screening from company reports. It never republishes the DSE's licensed constituent list.

fire.a: Financial Independence, Retire Early. It means having enough invested that its returns could pay your yearly costs, so paid work becomes a choice. Many people keep working after they reach it.

retire.q: Do I have to retire early?
retire.a: No. Most people use FIRE as a target for freedom: to change careers, start a business, care for family or work less. The plan shows when that choice could open up.

promise.q: Is my FIRE age a promise?
promise.a: No. It is a projection from the figures you enter and assumptions about returns and inflation. Markets and costs change, so the plan includes stress tests and you can update it at any time.

what.a: Assets, Capital and Earnings. Assets are what you own and owe. Capital is the part of your money that is invested or put to work. Earnings are your income, costs and savings. Together they decide how soon you could reach FIRE.

shares.q: Do I need to own shares?
shares.a: No. A FIRE plan can be built on savings certificates, sukuk, Islamic deposits, gold and other assets. Share tools are an extra for people who hold DSE stocks.

advice.a: No. analysisACE shows historical analysis for education. It never recommends buying, selling or holding anything, and the decision is always yours.

data.q: Where does the data come from?
data.a: Your household figures come from what you enter or import. Market figures come from the stock exchange, Bangladesh Bank and other public sources, and company reports. Every figure names its source. While analysisACE is in development, market pages run on clearly labelled demo data.

privacy.a: Yes. Only members of your household can see it. Account numbers and documents are encrypted, optional uses need your consent, and you can export or delete your data at any time.

language.q: Can I use it in Bangla?
language.a: Yes. Every page, notice and PDF statement is available in Bangla and English, with Bangla digits.

fire.scenariosIntro: Test the plan against a market fall, the replay of a past event, higher costs, stopping work earlier or higher inflation.
fire.scenarioAge: Reached at {age} ({change} years later than the plan)
fire.eventHint: The DSEX fall after it is applied to your listed shares.
fire.noEvents: No events in the library yet.
fire.paramHint: Leave empty for the usual size.
fire.monthlySavingsHint: From your income less costs, averaged over the last 12 months. Change it if it is not right.

goals.intro: Targets for net worth, money invested or FIRE age, and how close you are.
goals.onTrack: on track at the current pace
goals.addIntro: Give a target amount, or a target age for a FIRE goal.
goals.targetAmountHint: For net worth and invested-amount goals.
goals.savingsHint: For "Saved each month", the target is a monthly amount. Progress uses the average over the last 12 months of income less costs.

alerts.intro: Notices about your money, and how you want to receive them. Until an email provider is set up, emails are not sent.
alerts.settingsIntro: Each alert also shows here in the app. "Once a day" collects that alert into one email or notification each morning; "Straight away" sends each one as it happens.

describe.ALLOCATION_DRIFT: When an asset type moves outside the band you set.
describe.VOLATILITY: When your listed holdings move more than your limit.
describe.MATURITY_DUE: Before a holding matures, and before a government sukuk auction.
describe.REVALUATION_DUE: When a property or other asset needs a new value.
describe.MONTHLY_REPORT: A summary at the start of each month.
describe.SHARIAH_STATUS: When a stock you hold or watch changes Shariah status.
describe.REGIME_CHANGE: When the monthly macro regime label changes.
describe.SHOCK_EVENT: When a new event is published in the shock playbook.

notice.ALLOCATION_DRIFT: {asset_class} is {actual_pct}% of your portfolio. Your target is {target_pct}% with a band of {band_pct} points.
notice.VOLATILITY: Over the past year your listed holdings moved with an annualised volatility of {volatility_pct}%. Your limit is {limit_pct}%.
notice.SUKUK_AUCTION: {name} is scheduled for auction on {date} ({days} days from now).
notice.REVALUATION_DUE: {name} was last valued more than {months} months ago. Enter its current value to keep your net worth up to date.
notice.HAWL_APPROACHING: The Zakat date for {name} is {date} ({days} days from now).
notice.SHARIAH_STATUS_CHANGED: The Shariah status of {ticker} changed from {from_status} to {to_status}.
notice.REGIME_CHANGED: The macro regime label changed from {previous} to {label}.
notice.SHOCK_EVENT_PUBLISHED: A new event was added to the shock playbook: {title_en} ({date}).
notice.MONTHLY_REPORT_INCOME: Spending in {month}: {spending}. Income: {income}, left after costs: {savings}. Net worth: {net_worth}.

community.intro: See how your savings rate and FIRE progress compare with people of a similar age. Anonymous and opt-in.
community.consentBody: Turn on "Anonymous community comparisons" in your account. Only anonymous medians are shown, and only for groups large enough that no one can be picked out.
community.noPlan: The comparison uses your newest FIRE plan. Make one first.
community.noBand: Your age is outside the groups
community.tooSmall: The group comparison appears once at least {n} people of your age band have joined.

household.intro: The people whose money you track together, and what each may do.
household.createIntro: A household holds your accounts, assets and costs. You can add family members later.
household.name: Household name
household.membersIntro: Owners manage members. Editors add and change records. Viewers only look.
household.hawlHint: The day each year Zakat falls due (hawl).
household.addIntro: Add a child or a relative without a login, or share with someone who already has an analysisACE account.
household.emailHint: Only to share with an existing account.
household.anotherIntro: For example, your parents' money kept separately. Switch between households at the top of each page.

returnBasis.OWN_SUKUK_AND_DEPOSITS: From the rates of your own sukuk and deposits

marketCheck.intro: Your listed shares and funds against the market layer: Shariah share, rate sensitivity, how they moved in past shocks, and a dividend purification estimate.
marketCheck.shockIntro: Value-weighted moves of your current holdings after each published event.
marketCheck.purificationIntro: Dividends received in the last 12 months × each company's non-permissible income ratio. Ask your scholar how to give it.
marketCheck.unknownRatio: Dividends where the ratio is not known: {amount}
marketCheck.empty: No listed shares or funds yet. Add them under Accounts and holdings.

nav.shortcutsIntro: Everything in My money, grouped by what you want to do.

income.intro: Record what the household earns. Together with your costs it shows what is left to save each month.
income.byMonthHint: Income less costs for each month with records.
income.recurringIntro: A salary or rent is added on its due dates automatically.
income.importIntro: A CSV with the columns date, amount, kind, and optionally note and member. Kind is one of SALARY, BUSINESS, RENT, REMITTANCE, PROFIT, DIVIDEND or OTHER. Member is a name from your household.

setup.checklistIntro: {done} of {total} steps done. Each one makes your FIRE plan more accurate.
setup.intro: The basics in one form. Leave out anything you do not know yet; you can change everything later on the usual pages.
setup.viewerOnly: You can view this household but not change it. Ask an owner or editor to fill in the quick start.
setup.submit: Save and see my FIRE picture
setup.youIntro: Your FIRE age is worked out from this.
setup.alreadyDone: Already recorded. A new value replaces it.
setup.incomeIntro: What comes in each month after tax, from salary or other regular work.
setup.monthlyIncomeHint: Added as monthly income from the 1st of this month. A second earner can be added on the Income page.
setup.alreadyIncome: You already have income records. This adds another monthly income.
setup.costsIntro: Fixed costs repeat every month from the 1st of this month. Day-to-day costs are entered once as this month's estimate; keep recording them on the Costs page.
setup.alreadyCosts: You already have cost records. Amounts here are added to them.
setup.variable: Day to day, this month's estimate
setup.savingsIntro: Totals are enough for now. Each becomes one holding you can split up later.
setup.alreadySavings: You already have holdings. Amounts here are added as new holdings.
setup.savingsLater: Shares are best imported from your broker statement on the Accounts page. Gold and land go on the Property page.

holdingCompany.title: About this company
holdingCompany.intro: How the company behind this holding has been screened, and how its price has historically moved with interest rates.
holdingCompany.rateHint: Typical move in the share price when the 91-day T-bill yield rose one point, from past weekly data. History, not a forecast.

push.title: Notifications on this device
push.intro: Get a browser notification for alerts set to "Browser notification" or "Both" above. Turn it on separately on each phone or computer.
push.failed: Notifications could not be turned on. Try again, or check the browser's site settings.
push.notAvailable: Browser notifications are not switched on for analysisACE yet.

state.unsupported: This browser cannot show notifications from websites. On an iPhone, add analysisACE to the home screen first.
state.blocked: Notifications are blocked for this site. Allow them in the browser's site settings, then come back.
state.off: Notifications are off on this device.
state.on: Notifications are on for this device.

market.demoNotice: Figures marked as demo data are synthetic and only show how the page works.

shariah.intro: Every screened company, its status and the method behind it. analysisACE runs its own screen; it does not show the DSE's DSES constituents.

screen.stage1None: Business activity has not been classified yet.

scores.insufficient: Fewer than 104 usable weeks, so no score is shown.

rates.subject: Name

events.subject: Name
events.similarIntro: Other events of the same type, newest first.
events.noSimilar: No other events of this type yet.
events.companyEmpty: No event data for this company yet.

macro.intro: A weekly summary of yields, inflation, the taka, remittance, oil and the DSE, written from stored data. Every figure shows its source.
macro.empty: No note has been published yet.
macro.notFound: There is no published note for that week.

regime.title: Macro regime
regime.intro: A rules-based label for each month from the yield trend, inflation and oil, and how sectors have done in past months with the same label.
regime.label: Regime
regime.sectorsTitle: Sectors in past months with this label
regime.sectorsIntro: Average monthly return and share of months with a gain, in past months that carried the same label.
regime.noSectors: No past months share this label yet.

data.title: Data
data.intro: Failed quality checks wait here. Bad rows are not stored until the issue is handled.
data.open: {n, plural, =0 {Nothing open} one {# open} other {# open}}
data.metalIntro: Enter the price a gram for the day (Q9: manual entry). A price far from the previous day's is refused.
data.csvIntro: Columns: code, date (YYYY-MM-DD), value. A file with any bad row is refused whole.
data.actionsIntro: Bonus, rights and splits rewrite the stock's adjusted prices at once.
data.ratioHint: Bonus 0.10 for 10%; split 2 for 1:2; rights shares per share held.
data.amountHint: Rights issue price, or cash dividend a share.
data.analyticsIntro: Screen, scores, event metrics, basket and regime run every night. Run them now after loading data.

shariah.title: Shariah screen administration
shariah.intro: Figures are screened only after a reviewer has checked them against the report. Overrides need a reason and are audited.
shariah.pending: {n, plural, one {# period to review} other {# periods to review}}
shariah.overrideIntro: Sets the shown status by board decision. Choose "No override" to go back to the screen's result.
shariah.note: Note shown on the company page
shariah.financialsIntro: Enter figures from the report in taka. Leave a figure empty when the report does not state it. Saved figures wait for review.

events.title: Shock events
events.intro: Published events appear in the shock playbook. Publishing computes the event's metrics and alerts users who asked for it.
events.slugHint: Lower case letters, digits and dashes, for example lng-fire-2026.

notes.title: Weekly macro notes
notes.intro: A draft is written every week from stored data. Edit the text, then publish each language.
notes.bodyHint: Lines starting with "## " become headings and "- " become list items.

audit.title: Audit log and jobs
audit.intro: Every admin action, override and access change. Entries name user ids, never emails.

bankFlags.title: Bank notices
bankFlags.intro: A notice appears beside a household's deposits at that bank. Keep it factual and give a source; it must not tell anyone what to do.
bankFlags.bankHint: Exactly as the bank appears in product and holding records.
bankFlags.deleteBody: The notice will no longer appear beside deposits at this bank.

firm.intro: Weekly reports under your firm's name, data exports and API access for your team.
firm.reportIntro: The published weekly macro note as a PDF with your firm's logo, name and disclaimer, ready to send to clients.
firm.noReport: No weekly note has been published yet.
firm.exportsIntro: analysisACE's own Shariah screen and the rate-sensitivity scores as CSV, with their date and the disclaimer.
firm.name: Name
firm.emailHint: The person needs an analysisACE account with this email.
firm.keysIntro: Read-only access to the same data for your own systems. Each key has its own limit per minute and is logged by day.
firm.keyOnce: Copy this key now. It will not be shown again; only a fingerprint of it is stored.
firm.keyFacts: Created {created} · last used {used} · {limit} calls a minute
firm.apiHowToBody: Send the key in the X-API-Key header. Every answer includes as_of and sources. These endpoints are read-only:
firm.usageIntro: Calls per key and endpoint over the last 30 days.
firm.brandingIntro: Shown on every page of your weekly report, next to analysisACE's own disclaimer.
firm.disclaimerHint: Printed at the foot of each page of the report. Up to 1,000 characters.
firm.logoHint: PNG or JPEG, under 300 KB. It is resized to fit 600 pixels.
firm.noLogo: No logo yet; the report shows the firm's name.
firm.ownScreen: Shariah results come from analysisACE's own screening of company reports, never from the DSE's licensed constituent list.

admin.title: Firms
admin.intro: Firm accounts for brokerages, asset managers and Islamic banks.
admin.name: Firm name
admin.createIntro: The first admin must already have an analysisACE account. They can add the rest of the team.
